title: Measurements
text:
Stomata are microscopic pores on leaf surfaces, each flanked by a pair of guard cells. Their geometry is a key indicator of plant physiology: stomatal size and aperture regulate gas exchange (CO₂/O₂) and water loss (transpiration). Accurate morphometric measurements allow researchers to:

Compare stomatal morphology across genotypes, species, or treatments
Quantify stress responses (drought, heat) through pore aperture changes
Estimate stomatal conductance from geometric proxies

title: Measurements
text:
Trait Definitions
PSCA reports every measurement in both pixels and micrometres (µm). Pixel-to-micrometre conversion uses the calibration constant:
\[
\text{PX\_TO\_UM} = \frac{50.0\,\mu\text{m}}{451.3958\,\text{px}} \approx 0.1108\,\mu\text{m/px}
\]






Note



This calibration is specific to the microscope and objective used during image acquisition. If you use different optics, update PX_TO_UM in src/extract_traits.py.




1. Major Axis Length (major_axis_len_um)


📏 Major Axis — Full Stoma Length


The longest dimension of the minimum-area bounding rectangle fitted around the stoma mask. This corresponds to the longitudinal axis of the stoma, typically oriented parallel to the epidermal cell rows.


stoma_major_length_px = max(rect_width, rect_height) → × PX_TO_UM


How it is computed: cv2.minAreaRect() fits the tightest possible rotated rectangle around the stoma polygon. The longer of the two rectangle sides is taken as the major axis.
Biological meaning: Reflects overall stoma size. Larger stomata are associated with polyploidy, shade adaptation, and certain stress responses.



2. Minor Axis Length (minor_axis_len_um)


📏 Minor Axis — Full Stoma Width


The length of the minor axis line (perpendicular to the major axis) where it intersects the full stoma outline. Measured by projecting the minor-axis direction through the stoma polygon.


stoma_minor_length_px = minor_axis_line ∩ stoma_polygon → length → × PX_TO_UM


How it is computed:

The minor axis direction is extracted from the bounding rectangle angle.
An infinitely long line is cast through the stoma centroid along that direction.
The intersection of this line with the stoma polygon gives the chord length = minor axis.

Biological meaning: Width of the closed stoma. Together with the major axis, this gives a shape index (eccentricity / aspect ratio).



3. Pore Minor Length (pore_minor_len_um)


🔵 Pore Width — Aperture Diameter


The width of the central pore (aperture) measured along the same minor axis direction as above. PSCA detects the pore as a separate segmentation class and intersects it with the same minor axis line.


center_minor_length_px = minor_axis_line ∩ pore_polygon → length → × PX_TO_UM


How it is computed: The model segments the pore as class 0 (center) and the full stoma as class 1. The pore polygon is intersected with the same minor axis line used for the stoma.
Biological meaning: The most ecophysiologically important trait — directly proportional to stomatal conductance (g_s). A wider pore = higher gas exchange and transpiration.



4. Guard Cell Width (guard_cell_width_um)


🟢 Guard Cell Width — Thickness of One Guard Cell


Estimated as half the difference between the stoma width and the pore width along the minor axis. Represents the radial thickness of a single guard cell.


guard_cell_width_px = (stoma_minor_length_px − pore_minor_length_px) / 2 → × PX_TO_UM


How it is computed: Since the minor axis passes through both guard cells symmetrically, the stoma width = pore width + 2 × guard cell width.
Biological meaning: Guard cell thickness correlates with turgor potential and mechanical properties of the cell wall. Thicker guard cells tend to open with less turgor.

title: Measurements
Inference Pipeline
text:
PSCA is a containerised batch pipeline that:

Downloads images from CESNET S3 storage
Runs YOLOv11 instance segmentation on each image
Extracts geometric traits from the segmentation masks
Saves results to a CSV and uploads it back to S3

The pipeline runs as a Kubernetes Job — no local GPU required.

title: Inference Pipeline
text:
Step-by-Step

Step 1 — Model Download
If the model is not already cached at MODEL_PATH (/tmp/best.pt by default), it is downloaded from S3 at startup:
if S3_MODEL_KEY and not os.path.exists(MODEL_PATH):
    s3.download_file(S3_BUCKET, S3_MODEL_KEY, MODEL_PATH)
The model key is configured via the S3_MODEL_KEY environment variable.



Step 2 — Image Discovery
The S3 bucket is paginated to find all .jpg / .jpeg / .png files under the configured prefix:
paginator = s3.get_paginator('list_objects_v2')
pages = paginator.paginate(Bucket=S3_BUCKET, Prefix=TILE_PREFIX)
Default prefix: Ostatni/Stomata/extracted/



Step 3 — Parallel Download + Inference
Images are processed in batches of 100 to limit memory usage. Within each batch, images are downloaded concurrently using a 16-worker thread pool:
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=FETCH_WORKERS) as executor:
    futures = [executor.submit(download_image, s3, key) for key in batch_keys]
    for future in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures):
        key, img = future.result()
        if img is not None:
            res = process_image(model, img, image_name)






Note



YOLO inference itself runs sequentially on the GPU. Only image downloading is parallelised — this hides S3 network latency behind GPU compute time.





Step 4 — Trait Extraction
For each image, process_image() in extract_traits.py:

Runs YOLO inference → gets segmentation masks + class labels
Separates masks into stoma (class 1) and pore (class 0) lists
For each stoma, finds the matching pore (containment check → nearest-neighbour fallback)
Computes the minor axis via cv2.minAreaRect() and shapely intersection
Returns a list of measurement dicts

See the Measurements page for full trait definitions.



Step 5 — Output & Upload
Results are collected into a pandas DataFrame, saved to a local CSV, then uploaded to S3:
S3_OUTPUT_KEY = "Ostatni/Stomata/stomata_traits.csv"
Intermediate saves happen every 1000 images to guard against job interruption.

section: ☁️ CESNET S3 Cloud Storage Connection Protocol
text:
☁️ CESNET S3 Cloud Storage Connection Protocol
Goal: Connect our team’s cloud storage (CESNET S3) to your local computer so it appears as a regular folder. This allows you to drag-and-drop files from tools like Fiji, Excel, or RStudio directly to the cloud without using the browser.

title: Plant Stomata Counter-Analyser (PSCA)
text:
🛑 Step 0: Prerequisites (Install First)
Before you start, you need two things: Rclone (the connector software) and a FUSE driver (which lets Rclone “talk” to your file system).

Linux

Install Rclone: bash     sudo apt install rclone
FUSE: Usually pre-installed. If not: bash     sudo apt install fuse3



Windows

Install Rclone: Download the Rclone zip file, unzip it, and place rclone.exe somewhere safe (e.g., C:\rclone\). Add this folder to your system PATH.
Install WinFsp: Download and install WinFsp. Crucial: Rclone cannot mount a drive on Windows without this.



macOS

Install Rclone: Open Terminal and run: bash     brew install rclone (Requires Homebrew)
Install macFUSE: Download and install macFUSE.

Note: On newer Macs (M1/M2/M3), you may need to enable kernel extensions in Recovery Mode for macFUSE to work. Alternatively, verify if fuse-t is a suitable replacement for your version.

title: Plant Stomata Counter-Analyser (PSCA)
text:
⚙️ Step 1: Configure the Connection (All Platforms)
This step is the same for everyone. Open your terminal (Command Prompt on Windows) and run:
rclone config
Follow the interactive menu using the Team Credentials (ask the Project Lead for keys):

n (New remote)
Name: cesnet_s3
Storage: Select Amazon S3 Compliant Storage.
Provider: Select Ceph.
env_auth: false
access_key_id: [Enter Team Access Key]
secret_access_key: [Enter Team Secret Key]
endpoint: https://s3.cl4.du.cesnet.cz
acl: private
Save: Press y.

title: Plant Stomata Counter-Analyser (PSCA)
text:
🔗 Step 2: Connect the Drive
Choose the instructions for your operating system below. 🐧 Option A: Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)
The One-Time Command:
# 1. Create the mount folder
mkdir ~/cesnet_cloud

# 2. Mount it (runs in background)
rclone mount s3_cesnet: ~/cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes --daemon
Make it Permanent (Auto-start on Login):
Open "Startup Applications".

Click Add.

Command:
```bash
rclone mount s3_cesnet: /home/YOUR_USER/cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes --daemon
```

🪟 Option B: Windows
The One-Time Command (PowerShell):
# 1. Create the folder (or pick a drive letter like Z:)
mkdir C:\cesnet_cloud

# 2. Mount it
rclone mount s3_cesnet: C:\cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes
Note: This terminal window must stay open. If you close it, the drive disconnects.
Make it Permanent (Auto-start on Login):
Create a new text file named mount_cesnet.bat.

Paste this code inside:

```batch
@echo off
start /b rclone mount s3_cesnet: Z: –vfs-cache-mode writes –no-console ```
(This mounts it as the Z: drive).
Press Win + R, type shell:startup, and press Enter.
Move your mount_cesnet.bat file into this folder. It will now run silently every time you log in.


🍎 Option C: macOS
The One-Time Command:
 - 1. Create the mount folder
mkdir ~/cesnet_cloud

 - 2. Mount it
rclone mount s3_cesnet: ~/cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes --daemon
Make it Permanent (Auto-start on Login):
Open "System Preferences" > "Users & Groups".

Select your user and go to the "Login Items" tab.

Click the "+" button and add a new script.

Create a script file (e.g., mount_cesnet.sh) with the following content:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
rclone mount s3_cesnet: /Users/YOUR_USER/cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes --daemon
```

Make it executable:
```bash
chmod +x /path/to/mount_cesnet.sh
```

Add this script to your login items.
Save the app as “Connect CESNET”.
Go to System Settings -> General -> Login Items and add “Connect CESNET” to the list.


⚠️ Important Best Practices
Don't Edit in Place: Avoid opening a huge video file directly from the cloud drive to edit. Copy it to your desktop first, edit, then copy it back. (Small text/image edits are fine).

Wait for the Upload: When you drag a file into the folder, it may take a few seconds to upload. Don't immediately shut down your computer.

If it freezes: If the folder stops responding (e.g., internet loss), unmount it:

    Linux: fusermount -u ~/cesnet_cloud

    Windows: Ctrl+C in the terminal or restart.

    Mac: umount ~/cesnet_cloud

text:
Following full batch deep-learning inference across all 3,253 micrographs on the CESNET GPU cluster, we performed preliminary statistical analysis of the extracted stomatal traits.
A critical consideration in this analysis is the hierarchical nested structure of the experimental system:

    Pop --> Plant

    style Cyt fill:#1e3a8a,color:#fff,stroke:#3b82f6,stroke-width:2px
    style Pop fill:#047857,color:#fff,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:2px
    style Plant fill:#b45309,color:#fff,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:2px
    style Photo fill:#374151,color:#fff,stroke:#9ca3af,stroke-width:2px






To account for non-independence, correlated error structures, and unequal sample sizes across natural populations, all key traits are evaluated using Linear Mixed-Effects Models (LMM) with Satterthwaite approximations for degrees of freedom:
\[\text{Trait}_{ijkl} = \mu + \text{Cytotype}_i + \text{LeafSide}_j + (\text{Cytotype} \times \text{LeafSide})_{ij} + u_{\text{population}(k)} + v_{\text{plant}(l \subset k)} + \epsilon_{ijkl}\]
where \(u_{\text{population}} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\text{pop}})\) and \(v_{\text{plant}} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\text{plant}})\).

title: Preliminary Trait Analysis & Mixed Models
text:
1. Stoma Length Analysis (Cell Size Proxy)
Stoma length (guard cell length along the major axis) is the classical morphological proxy for genome size and cell enlargement (gigas effect).

Mixed Model Fit


Show R code
# Filter images with well-focused stomata suitable for measurement
df_len <- df %>% filter(!is.na(ploidy_median_stoma_length_um))

# Linear mixed-effects model
m_len <- lmer(
  ploidy_median_stoma_length_um ~ cytotype * leaf_side + (1 | population) + (1 | population:plant_ID),
  data = df_len
)

# ANOVA table
anova_len <- anova(m_len)
kable(round(as.data.frame(anova_len), 3), caption = "Type III ANOVA with Satterthwaite's method for Stoma Length (µm)") %>%

NoteKey Biological Insights on Stoma Length




Clear Ploidy Separation (\(p < 0.001\)): Diploids (ory_2x: \(18.28\) µm, nat_2x: \(18.56\) µm) are significantly smaller than natural tetraploids (nat_4x: \(20.30\) µm), which in turn are substantially smaller than newly formed synthetic neotetraploids (neo_4x: \(23.52\) µm).

In contrast, established wild nat_4x exhibits an intermediate size (+9.4% over nat_2x), suggesting evolutionary cell size optimization or genome downsizing following polyploidization.
Leaf-Side Modulation (\(p < 0.001\)): Across all cytotypes, adaxial (upper surface) stomata are systematically \(0.35 - 0.86\) µm longer than abaxial stomata.

text:
6. Biophysical Traits: Maximum Stomatal Conductance (\(g_{s\max}\)) & Stomatal Pore Area Index (SPI)
Using the biophysical formulation of Franks & Farquhar (2001) and Sack & Buckley (2016), theoretical maximum stomatal conductance to water vapor (\(g_{s\max}\), \(\text{mol m}^{-2} \text{s}^{-1}\)) integrates stomatal density (\(D\)), guard cell depth (\(l \approx \text{guard cell width}\)), and maximum pore aperture area (\(a_{\max}\)):
\[g_{s\max} = \frac{d}{v} \cdot \frac{D \cdot a_{\max}}{l + \frac{\pi}{2}\sqrt{a_{\max}/\pi}}\]
where \(d = 2.49 \times 10^{-5} \ \text{m}^2 \text{s}^{-1}\) is water vapor diffusivity in air and \(v = 0.02446 \ \text{m}^3 \text{mol}^{-1}\) is molar volume at 25°C.

title: Preliminary Trait Analysis & Mixed Models
text:
7. Cell-Level Hierarchical Variance Decomposition (\(N = 51,460\) Stomata)
To test whether newly formed polyploids exhibit elevated cell-to-cell developmental noise (fluctuating asymmetry or developmental instability), we fit a fully nested hierarchical mixed-effects model directly to all \(51,460\) individually measured ploidy-suitable stomata:
\[\text{Length}_{ijklm} = \mu + \text{Cytotype}_i \times \text{LeafSide}_j + u_{\text{pop}(k)} + v_{\text{plant}(l \subset k)} + w_{\text{photo}(m \subset l)} + \epsilon_{ijklm}\]


Show R code
# Load full cell-level dataset if available
cell_file <- "data/stomata_traits_all_3253_stomata.csv"
if (file.exists(cell_file)) {
  df_cells <- read.csv(cell_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    filter(is_suitable_for_ploidy_sizing == TRUE | is_suitable_for_ploidy_sizing == "True") %>%
    mutate(
      cytotype = factor(cytotype, levels = c("ory_2x", "nat_2x", "nat_4x", "neo_4x")),
      leaf_side = factor(leaf_side, levels = c("abaxial", "adaxial")),
      population = factor(population),
      plant_ID = factor(plant_ID),
      image_name = factor(image_name)
    )

  m_cell <- lmer(
    stoma_major_um ~ cytotype * leaf_side + (1 | population) + (1 | population:plant_ID) + (1 | population:plant_ID:image_name),
    data = df_cells
  )

  # Extract variance components
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m_cell)) %>%
    select(grp, vcov, sdcor) %>%
    rename(Level = grp, Variance = vcov, StdDev = sdcor)

  kable(vc, digits = 3, caption = "Variance Component Decomposition across Hierarchical Levels for Stoma Length") %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))
}

title: Preliminary Trait Analysis & Mixed Models
text:
Conclusions

Enhanced Trait Extraction Engine:

The retrained YOLOv11 segmentation model (incorporating 175 background negative controls and active-learning crops) achieved mAP50 of 0.972 and Precision of 0.944, successfully eliminating false detections on plant cuticle.
Sub-pixel orthogonal intensity analysis resolved pore apertures down to sub-micron resolution and closed-pore longitudinal grooves.

Clear Evolutionary Differentiation:

Diploid Baseline: ory_2x (\(18.99\) µm) and nat_2x (\(19.20\) µm) maintain high density and small, tightly regulated stomata.
Neopolyploid Hyper-Expansion: neo_4x (\(24.52\) µm) displays massive cellular enlargement accompanied by a severe drop in stomatal density, leading to a theoretical conductance bottleneck (\(g_{s\max} = 0.718\)).
Post-Polyploid Evolutionary Downsizing: Established wild tetraploids (nat_4x, \(20.95\) µm) demonstrate evolutionary downsizing and density recovery, restoring high theoretical conductance (\(g_{s\max} = 0.902\)).

title: Stomata Measurement Precision QC App
text:
Overview & Purpose
In automated plant morphometry, the central question for downstream ecological and evolutionary analysis is: How precise is the automated measurement?
The Stomata Precision QC App provides researchers and collaborators with a dedicated, interactive web environment to directly evaluate: 1. Segmentation accuracy: Does the YOLO segmentation polygon tightly and faithfully follow the outer guard cell boundary and inner aperture? 2. Measurement axis alignment: Does the major axis strictly span between the two stomatal poles? Does the minor axis line pass through the exact center of maximum pore width? 3. Pore aperture precision: Is the central aperture opening accurately measured, even for challenging, narrow, or partially closed stomatal pores? 4. Ploidy suitability gate: Does the stoma meet strict biometric criteria for cell size comparison across ploidy levels (is_suitable_for_ploidy_sizing), or is it only valid for stomatal density counting? 5. Human ground-truth benchmarking: Using the built-in Digital Caliper Tool, researchers can manually measure stomata on screen and immediately quantify the model’s Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and bias in micrometres (\(\mu\text{m}\)).

title: Stomata Measurement Precision QC App
text:
Key Features & Interface Tour

1. High-Magnification Stoma Precision View
The primary workspace provides an interactive HTML5 canvas with continuous smooth zoom (\(1\times\) to \(8\times\)) and drag-to-pan navigation to closely inspect individual stomata at sub-pixel resolution.



Stoma Crop Precision view showing color-coded anatomical vectors, measurement indicators, and the reviewer inspector panel.



Vectorized Anatomical Overlays
The canvas overlays the mathematical measurement vectors calculated by the pipeline:

Stoma Body

Orthogonal chord through centroid (\(\mu\text{m}\))

\((L_{\text{minor}} - P_{\text{width}}) / 2\) (\(\mu\text{m}\))









Tip




Hold Space: Instantly hides all vector overlays to inspect the raw, unfiltered microscopy image.
Press X: Toggles CLAHE (Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization) to enhance faint guard cell walls in lower-contrast images.







2. Interactive Virtual Digital Caliper (C)
The app features an integrated Digital Caliper Tool allowing researchers to independently measure any anatomical dimension with precision crosshairs directly on the crop canvas.



Virtual Caliper in action: Click-and-drag crosshairs measure distance in micrometres and compare directly against the automated model measurement.



How to Benchmark Measurement Precision:

Click 📏 Digital Caliper (or press C).
Click and drag across the stoma poles (for length), across the stoma waist (for width), or across the pore opening.
The Caliper HUD displays:

Measured physical distance in \(\mu\text{m}\) (using the calibration \(\text{PX\_TO\_UM} \approx 0.1107675\,\mu\text{m/px}\)).
Quick buttons: Set Major, Set Minor, or Set Pore to record the ground truth comparison.

The system calculates the exact discrepancy: \[\Delta = \text{Model} - \text{Human}\quad (\mu\text{m})\] \[\text{Error } \% = \frac{|\text{Model} - \text{Human}|}{\text{Human}} \times 100\%\]





3. Panoramic Micrograph Field Explorer
Switching to the Micrograph Field tab allows researchers to step back and inspect the full \(3096 \times 4140\) px brightfield microscopy slide with all detected stomata annotated.



Full Micrograph Field view with annotated stoma badges and slide metadata.


Researchers can verify field-level characteristics: - Spatial distribution and clustering (Clark-Evans dispersion index) - Epidermal quality, focus variation across the leaf surface, air bubbles, and staining artifacts - Jump directly to any slide or plant ID from the left sidebar



4. Precision Benchmark Analytics Dashboard
The Precision Dashboard tab compiles real-time accuracy benchmarks across all reviewer evaluations and caliper measurements.



Precision Analytics Dashboard showing error benchmarks, MAE in micrometres, and reviewer audit progress.



Available Benchmarks & Telemetry:

Precision Classification Rate: Percentage of stomata verified as High Precision vs Minor Deviation vs Poor Measurement.
Mean Absolute Error (MAE): Average deviation in \(\mu\text{m}\) between automated model measurements and human digital caliper measurements for Major Axis, Minor Axis, and Pore Width.
Mean Bias: Identifies whether the automated model tends to systematically over- or under-estimate pore aperture or cell width.
Reviewer Progress & Audit Trail: Number of stomata reviewed per collaborator, median time per evaluation, and timestamps.
One-Click CSV Export: Direct download of precision.csv for statistical analysis in R or Python.

title: Stomata Measurement Precision QC App
text:
Cloud Architecture & Storage Integration
The review application operates entirely stateless inside the cluster, persisting all review data directly to the CESNET S3 Ceph object store (peg-bucket):
s3://peg-bucket/Ostatni/Stomata/Review/
├── manifest.json              # Full dataset manifest with geometric vectors
├── crops/                     # High-resolution 360x360 stoma crops (JPEG)
├── overviews/                 # Scaled panoramic field micrographs (JPEG)
└── decisions/                 # Reviewer decisions and caliper ground truth
    └── {item_id}/
        └── {reviewer}.json    # JSON audit record per item and reviewer
Because decisions are committed directly to S3 as individual JSON records, reviews are safely preserved across pod updates or restarts, and multiple team members can review simultaneously without conflicts.

Deployment & Maintenance
The app can be redeployed or updated with a single script:
bash deploy_stomata_review.sh
This updates the Kubernetes ConfigMap, applies the Deployment and Ingress specifications in k8s/stomata-review.yaml, and executes a zero-downtime rolling restart on the CESNET cluster.

title: Cloud Storage Setup
text:
ImportantCredentials



Ask the Project Lead for the team access_key_id and secret_access_key before starting. Do not share them via Slack or email — use a secure channel.
Goal: Mount the team’s CESNET S3 bucket as a local folder so you can drag-and-drop microscopy images and retrieve results without a browser.

title: Cloud Storage Setup
text:
Step 0 — Install Prerequisites
You need Rclone (the connector) and a FUSE driver (so Rclone can present the bucket as a folder).

🐧 Linux🪟 Windows🍎 macOS


sudo apt install rclone fuse3



Download Rclone for Windows, unzip, place rclone.exe in e.g. C:\rclone\, add to PATH.
Download and install WinFsp — required for mounting.



brew install rclone
Then download and install macFUSE.

Note (Apple Silicon): You may need to allow kernel extensions in Recovery Mode for macFUSE. Check if fuse-t works as an alternative on M1/M2/M3.

title: Cloud Storage Setup
text:
Step 2 — Mount the Drive

🐧 Linux🪟 Windows🍎 macOS


One-time:
mkdir ~/cesnet_cloud
rclone mount cesnet_s3: ~/cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes --daemon
Auto-start on login — open Startup Applications, click Add, and use this command:
rclone mount cesnet_s3: /home/YOUR_USER/cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes --daemon
Alternative — Direct S3FS Mount (peg-bucket):
mkdir -p ~/cesnet_new
s3fs peg-bucket ~/cesnet_new -o passwd_file=${HOME}/.passwd-s3fs -o url=https://s3.cl4.du.cesnet.cz -o use_path_request_style -o allow_other -o uid=$(id -u) -o gid=$(id -g)


One-time (PowerShell):
mkdir C:\cesnet_cloud
rclone mount cesnet_s3: C:\cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes

Keep this terminal open — closing it disconnects the drive.

Auto-start: Create mount_cesnet.bat with:
@echo off
start /b rclone mount cesnet_s3: Z: --vfs-cache-mode writes --no-console
Place the .bat file in shell:startup (Win + R → type shell:startup).


One-time:
mkdir ~/cesnet_cloud
rclone mount cesnet_s3: ~/cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes --daemon
Auto-start: Create mount_cesnet.sh:
#!/bin/bash
rclone mount cesnet_s3: /Users/YOUR_USER/cesnet_cloud --vfs-cache-mode writes --daemon
Make it executable (chmod +x mount_cesnet.sh) and add it in System Settings → General → Login Items.

title: Cloud Storage Setup
text:
⚠️ Best Practices






Warning



Don’t edit large files in place. Copy the file to your local desktop first, edit it there, then copy it back. Opening a multi-GB image directly from the cloud drive will be slow.








Tip



Wait for uploads. When you drag a file into cesnet_cloud/, give it a few seconds to finish uploading before shutting down your computer.


If the drive freezes (e.g. internet loss), unmount it:



Platform
Command




Linux
fusermount -u ~/cesnet_cloud


Windows
Ctrl+C in the terminal


macOS
umount ~/cesnet_cloud
